pairs.subject: native-shell-integration
pairs.evidence: src/features/browser/webview/WebviewPage.tsx:154 Commands that act on the page cross as tab ids and page-issued refs. The one free string, a URL, is checked by the native navigation whitelist gate, and the native side re-derives the page each hand acts on from its own tab table (webview.rs admit), while tab state follows a native-emitted event.

techniques.evidence: src/features/browser/webview/WebviewPage.tsx:154 Rule two: the typed URL is tested natively by policy::check_navigation (whitelist) before navigating. Fill, submit and pick pass through admit(), which reads the tab's current URL from native state rather than trusting the caller.

src/features/browser/browserStore.ts:258 Tab state is owned natively and fanned out on the browser-tabs event. The store seeds from browser_webview_list and renders, and a failed subscribe does not latch.

src/features/browser/webview/WebviewPage.tsx:4 The host is an opaque, owned (not transparent or always-on-top) window that the user types into. That is the technique's 'meant to be interacted with' exclusion. Its visibility is derived in one place (hostVisibility.ts:82).

src-tauri/src/browser_bridge/webview/mod.rs:130 The page host is built on all three hosts through one parent() call with no cfg, so no host lacks the capability. A missing backend refuses with its own NoBackend code.

src/features/browser/twinDraftLane.ts:296 Pick mode is armed inside the page by injected hands, not by a product overlay placed over a foreign app, so no point query can hit the product's own surface.
src/features/browser/twinDraftLane.ts:252 Text is inserted by setting the field value directly (page_fill), not by synthesizing keystrokes or chords, so no keyboard-layout resolution is involved.
